subject: SOC 2: sampling approach & tenant boundaries for Dedicated pools and VPC/private installs
body:
From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@enterprisebank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@enterprisebank.com
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 coverage question — dedicated pools + VPC/private installs

Hi Jonas,

Quick question from our InfoSec intake: your SOC 2 Type II report we received references the control environment for Redwood's hosted service. We need to confirm how the report and sampling apply to: (a) Dedicated GPU pools (Redwood-managed but single-tenant) and (b) Private/VPC or on-prem installs where Redwood provides the control plane but the customer operates networking.

Specifically: do the testing population/sampling in the report include dedicated pools, and can we rely on a bridge letter to cover any timing gaps? Also, for Private/VPC deployments — is the control scope limited to Redwood-managed components (control plane + agents) and excluded for customer-managed infra?

We have an audit kickoff next week, so a concise mapping would be ideal.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Holt
Senior Information Security Manager
Enterprise Bank

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@enterprisebank.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question — dedicated pools + VPC/private installs

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Laura (InfoSec) and Karthik (Infra) to confirm specifics; copy of our 2025-06 SOC 2 Type II attached and a quick scoping matrix.

High-level reply:
- Dedicated pools: Redwood-managed dedicated capacity is included in the control environment tested in the SOC 2 report when the customer has purchased Dedicated and the underlying service components are operated by Redwood. Sampling is performed at the control population level (e.g., change management tickets, access reviews) across service instances; dedicated instances that are part of Redwood's managed estate were within the auditor's population for the covered period.
- Private/VPC (managed control plane): When Redwood is operating the control plane components (agents, control plane services) and clearly documented in the Sys Description, those components are typically in-scope. Customer-managed network infrastructure or on-prem hardware that the customer owns is generally excluded and covered via complementary user-entity controls (CUECs).
- Bridge letters: we can provide a dated bridge letter for the period between the end of the report and today to cover continuing assertion of controls; template attached.

Laura / Karthik — can you confirm the sampling approach we gave the auditor (statements about population vs samples) and whether we have a caveat for particular private on-prem installs that were explicitly excluded? If helpful I can share the customer's auditor contact (Michael Lee) to loop in.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 10:02 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:

> Hi Sara and team,
>
> Thanks for the question — I’ll be concise and include practical language you can use with your auditor.
>
> 1) Scope and service boundaries
> - 'Hosted' (multi-tenant) and 'Dedicated' (Redwood-managed single-tenant pools) are both part of Redwood's managed service boundary where the same control framework applies. For Dedicated pools that are operated by Redwood (we manage provisioning, patching, access), those systems were included in the population the auditor sampled from during the Type II period. That means code release controls, incident management, access provisioning, and logical environment separation are asserted in the report.
>
> 2) Sampling methodology (practical wording)
> - Auditor approach: they select a sampling population derived from our service inventory and then perform attribute testing on a statistically representative subset. For customers asking whether 'their' dedicated instance was sampled: auditors do not typically guarantee sampling of a particular instance; rather they provide assurance over the control population. Recommended language: "The report represents the auditor's testing over Redwood's stated population of managed service instances for the period [period dates]. Specific dedicated pools are part of the population but may or may not have been individually sampled; the report is an assertion over the control environment and practices applied to those pools."
>
> 3) Private / VPC / On-prem guidance
> - If Redwood maintains the control plane components (authentication, orchestration, agents) we include those items in-scope. If customers operate their own host/network layer (on-prem or pure customer-managed VPC resources), those components are out-of-scope and the customer should provide CUECs to their auditor.
>
> 4) Bridge letter and mapping artifacts
> - We can provide: (a) a bridge letter asserting continuity from report end-date to present, (b) a SOC 2 scoping matrix mapping Redwood systems to control categories, and (c) a Sys Description extract for the customer's auditor. Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-06_report.pdf, SOC2_scoping_matrix.xlsx, bridge_letter_template.docx.
>
> 5) Next steps for audit kickoff
> - If your auditor needs direct confirmation, we’re OK with a short, scheduled call with our audit liaison. If you want an explicit statement that a particular dedicated instance was part of the auditor's sample, we can ask the auditor but they rarely confirm instance-level sampling.
>
> Hope this helps — happy to reword for auditor consumption if you send the specific request text.
>
> Best,
> Laura Bennett
> Director, Information Security & Compliance
> Redwood Inference
>

From: Michael Lee <michael.lee@auditfirm.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: sara.holt@enterprisebank.com
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question — dedicated pools + VPC/private installs

Laura/Jonas — quick confirmation from the auditor side:
- We are confirming population-level testing. Our report language will not single out an individual customer's dedicated instance as 'sampled' except in rare circumstances.
- For Private/VPC deployments: we test the control activities performed by Redwood (control plane components). Customer-owned infrastructure remains the customer's responsibility and should be addressed via CUECs.
- Bridge letters: we will accept a Redwood-dated bridge letter for continuity; the usual disclaimers on no material control changes apply.

If Enterprise Bank wants an auditor call, I'm available during the audit kickoff window.

Regards,
Michael Lee
Senior Manager, IT Audit
Northwest Assurance Partners
